newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar marginally firmer, trade quiet.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar marginally firmer, trade quiet.

text.p: Trading in London white sugar futures was subdued on Thursday with mainly flat-price buying of the spot August contract accounting for the thin volume.
One broker team was cited on the buy side, with the resulting strength in the market balanced by commission house sales. Traders said it was unclear who was behind the business.

Activity in London was not helped by the lacklustre performance in New York, where the benchmark July raws contract was confined to a five-point range and failed to break through nearby support at 11.00 cents/lb.
Both markets are expected to be quiet next week as players will be gathering in New York for the Sugar Dinner on Wednesday.
At 1535 GMT August was up 50 cents at $318.40, 10 cents off its intraday high, and October was up 50 cents at $308.20. Volume totalled 1,244 lots.

Little was reported in the way of fresh fundamental news although traders continued to look for news of white sugar imports into Russia, in addition to the hefty raws shipments into the Black Sea region.

Technical analysts said August would have to edge higher and test $319 or $320 before a downward correction was likely to occur. The position is seen as well supported at $316.60, Thursday's intraday low.
Trading stayed extremely quiet on the Paris market with just 80 lots of August on the board. The position was 70 cents weaker at $317.60.
